content: The provided text appears to be a list of references from various studies and articles related to pharmaceutical pricing, healthcare policies, and drug procurement systems. 1. The study by Németh et al. (2019) examines how price negotiations influence public procurement costs and access to eight innovative cancer medications in Mexico, a middle-income country. The findings are published in Value in Health Regional Issues. 2. Németh, Szigeti, and Pusztai (2015) conducted an analysis of the generic medicine market in Hungary, providing recommendations to improve its effectiveness. This report was published by the World Health Organization. 3. Nguyen, Kaplan, Laing, and Press (2008) reviewed policy options to promote the use of generic medicines in developing and transitional countries. Their findings were published by the World Health Organization in Geneva. 4. Olga et al. (2014) investigated the economic impacts of new public pharmaceutical policies in Greece, focusing on price reductions and cost-sharing rates. The results were published in Value in Health Regional Issues. 5. Paradis et al. (2009) explored the impact of generic substitution of topiramate on healthcare costs, translating the Canadian experience to four European countries. The findings were presented in Value in Health. 6. Parkinson et al. (2015) conducted an international review of disinvestment and value-based purchasing strategies for pharmaceuticals, published in Pharmacoeconomics. 7. Parlar-Chun and Malek (2019) demonstrated how price transparency can reduce the cost of seizure management among pediatric residents, as published in the Journal of Investigative Medicine. 8. Patel et al. (2011) analyzed the impact of generic drug discount programs on managed care organizations, with findings published in the American Journal of Pharmacy Benefits. 9. Petrou (2016) examined the long-term effects of tendering on the prices of branded pharmaceutical products, with results published in Health Policy and Technology. 10. Petrou and Talias (2014) evaluated the use of tendering as a reimbursement tool for pharmaceuticals in Cyprus' public health sector, as published in Health Policy and Technology. 11. Piniazjko et al. (2018) studied the implementation of external reference pricing, reimbursement programs, and health technology assessments in Ukraine's pharmaceutical system, with findings published in Pharmacia. 12. Prada et al. (2018) analyzed the increase in pharmaceutical public expenditure in Colombia following direct price control, questioning whether it improved access or induced demand. The study was published in Cost Effectiveness and Resource Allocation. 13. Puig-Junoy (2007) investigated the impact of generic reference pricing interventions in the statin market, with findings published in Health Policy. 14. Puig-Junoy (2010) reviewed the effects of European pharmaceutical price regulation on generic price competition, as published in Pharmacoeconomics. 15. Puig-Junoy and Moreno-Torres (2010) explored how generic firms and public purchasers in Spain respond to consumer price differences under reference pricing, with results published in Health Policy. 16. Qendri et al. (2019) analyzed the pricing of HPV vaccines in European tender-based settings, with findings published in the European Journal of Health Economics. 17. Raftery (2010) critiqued the multiple sclerosis risk-sharing scheme in the UK, describing it as a costly failure in the BMJ. 18. Rainova et al. (2013) reviewed the application of international reference pricing in Ukraine's pilot hypertension reimbursement scheme, with findings published in Value in Health. 19. Rothberg et al. (2004) shared experiences with a medicines reference-pricing model in South Africa, as published in the South African Medical Journal. 20. Roughead et al. (2018) examined pricing policies for generic medicines in Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, and Singapore, focusing on the influence of patent expiry on atorvastatin prices. The study was published in the WHO South-East Asia Journal. 21. Roy (2013) discussed the implementation of an essential medicines policy in public health facilities in Delhi, India, to provide low-cost, quality medicines. The findings were published in the International Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research. 22. Russo and McPake (2010) conducted a public health and economic study of pharmaceutical markets and price determinants in urban Mozambique, as published in Health Policy and Planning. 23. Sae Wong et al. (2010) analyzed a drug cost containment policy at a hospital in southern Thailand, with findings published in Value in Health. 24. Sahay and Jaikumar (2016) studied the impact of pharmaceutical price regulation on access to essential medicines in India, focusing on the effects of a drug price control order on sales volume. 25. Sakshaug et al. (2007) investigated the switching of statins in Norway following a new reimbursement policy, with findings published in the British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology. 26. Sanderson et al. (2015) proposed a framework to enhance procurement and supply chain management practices in the NHS, synthesizing theoretical and empirical literature. 27. Sarol Jesus (2014) evaluated the effect of government-mediated access pricing on the availability of drugs in retail stores in the Philippines from 2009 to 2011, as published in Acta Medica Philippina. 28. Schneeweiss et al. (2004) assessed net health plan savings from reference pricing for ACE inhibitors in elderly British Columbia residents, as published in Medical Care. 29. Sigulem and Zucchi (2009) examined the impact of joint drug purchases by a hospital network on e-procurement in Brazil's healthcare system, as published in the Revista Panamericana de Salud Pública. 30. Silvestri et al. (2016) conducted a systematic review on the impact of price display on provider ordering, with findings published in the Journal of Hospital Medicine. 31. Squarize Chagas (2012) analyzed the impact of tax substitution on pharmaceutical product prices in São Paulo, Brazil, as published in the Brazilian Review of Economics. 32. Stadhouders et al. (2019) reviewed effective healthcare cost-containment policies, with findings published in Health Policy. 33. Stargardt (2010) studied the impact of reference pricing on switching behavior and healthcare utilization in Germany's statin market, as published in the European Journal of Health Economics. 34. Stargardt (2011) modeled pharmaceutical price changes in Germany as a function of competition and regulation, with findings published in Applied Economics. 35. Steyn et al. (2007) evaluated the influence of a new reference-based pricing system in South Africa on the prevalence and cost of antidiabetic medicines, as published in the International Journal of Pharmacy Practice. 36. Suh et al. (2018) analyzed the effects of a price cut reform on the cost and utilization of antidiabetic drugs in Korea, using national health insurance database data, as published in BMC Health Services Research. 37. Timonen et al. (2013) reviewed lessons learned from generic substitution in Finland between 2003 and 2008, as published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Services Research. 38. Tordoff et al. (2005) evaluated price management strategies for hospital pharmaceuticals in New Zealand, with findings published in Value in Health. 39. Toulémon (2017) provided evidence on the effects of group purchasing on hospital medicine prices, as published in HAL. 40. Ubeda et al. (2007) studied the impact of generic and reference-based pricing policies on antidepressant utilization in primary care in Spain, as published in Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology. 41. Van Haeren et al. (2009) analyzed public tendering for off-patent pharmaceuticals in Belgium, focusing on the simvastatin case, as published in Value in Health. 42. Vandoros and Kanavos (2013) revisited the generics paradox, providing empirical evidence from regulated markets, as published in Applied Economics. 43. Vogler et al. (2017) shared lessons learned from tendering for off-patent outpatient medicines in Belgium, Denmark, and the Netherlands, as published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Services Research. 44. Vrijens et al. (2010) examined the reference price system and socioeconomic differences in the use of low-cost drugs, as published in the KCE Reports. 45. Wang et al. (2015) analyzed short-term differences in drug prices after implementing the national essential medicines system in rural Jiangxi Province, China, as published in the Indian Journal of Pharmacology. 46. Wouters et al. (2019) studied the impact of pharmaceutical tendering on prices and market concentration in South Africa over a 14-year period, as published in Social Science & Medicine. 47. Yang et al. (2017) evaluated the impact of the zero-markup drug policy on hospitalization expenditure in western rural China, as published in Tropical Medicine & International Health. 48. Zhou et al. (2015) assessed the financial impact of the zero-markup policy for essential drugs on patients in county hospitals in western rural China, as published in PLOS ONE.
